strengths: Compelling conceptual motivation: The paper provides a clear and insightful perspective on why predicting dense point trajectories directly is significantly more physically grounded and computationally efficient than relying on RGB pixel video generation.

Well-designed technical architecture: Adapting latent flow matching and spatio-temporal transformer blocks (with trajectory VAE and DINOv2 conditioning) provides an effective generative formulation capable of capturing multi-modal future dynamics across the full scene.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: The method is rigorously evaluated across diverse domains (robotics in LIBERO, physics simulations in Kubric, and real-world videos in Physics101/Physion), benchmarking against both trajectory forecasters (ATM, Tra-MoE, Track2Act) and large-scale video foundation models (WAN, SVD, LTX).

Insightful modality ablation: The controlled comparison between trajectory latents and RGB latents of comparable dimensionality (Table 6) strongly validates the core hypothesis that pixel generation overhead degrades motion plausibility.

Sound evaluation metrics: The inclusion of distribution-level metrics (FVMD, scene-wise FVMD(S)) alongside physical plausibility metrics (LRTL for rigidity) and user studies provides a multifaceted assessment of trajectory quality.
weaknesses: Downstream policy evaluation is missing: Prior robotics baselines (ATM, Tra-MoE) evaluate policy task success rate when conditioned on predicted trajectories. Demonstrating whether the lower MSE/higher diversity directly benefits downstream policy execution would substantially strengthen the practical impact.

Handling of occlusions and track terminations: The paper represents trajectories purely as 2D pixel coordinates $(x_t, y_t)$ over fixed time horizons without explicit visibility or occlusion modeling, which could limit performance when objects undergo heavy occlusion or leave the camera frustum.

Pseudo ground-truth reliance on real-world datasets: In Physics101, ground truth tracks are extracted using CoTracker3; while tracking quality is high, potential tracker failure modes may affect the ground-truth fidelity and evaluation accuracy.
Evaluation scale on real-world in-the-wild videos is relatively constrained, with Physics101 and Physion mostly capturing controlled physical setups rather than complex real-world scenes.

strengths: Compelling conceptual premise: generating dense 2D point trajectories directly via flow matching instead of synthesizing RGB pixels provides strong inductive biases (object permanence, temporal consistency) while avoiding the heavy computational and representational overhead of pixel synthesis.
Thorough comparative evaluation against both trajectory baselines (ATM, Tra-MoE, Track2Act) and major video foundation models (WAN 14B/1.3B, SVD, LTX, DynamicCrafter), including fine-tuned variants.

Insightful controlled modality ablation (Table 6) that fixes the architecture and compares RGB generation against trajectory generation under comparable latent dimensionality, convincingly demonstrating that the trajectory modality is inherently better suited for physical motion modeling.

Comprehensive evaluation protocol using complementary distributional and physical plausibility metrics (FVMD, image-conditioned FVMD(S), Best-of-K MSE, and the low-rank rigidity metric LRTL) alongside a user study.
Extensive implementation details, ablation studies on model scale, training on pseudo-ground truth (CoTracker3), and detailed compute expenditure documentation in the appendix.
weaknesses: No downstream policy evaluation on robotics tasks: the paper compares against ATM and Tra-MoE on LIBERO strictly in terms of trajectory MSE. Given that those baselines were developed primarily for robotic manipulation policy learning, demonstrating that the generated trajectory grids actually improve policy success rates would have significantly strengthened the paper's impact.

Inconsistent benefit of the trajectory VAE across benchmarks: while the VAE improves performance on Kubric and LIBERO, it degrades performance on Physics101 (Table 14: 28.62 MSE without VAE vs. 31.67 with VAE), which partially undermines the claim that a latent representation is fundamentally necessary for trajectory generation.

Limited real-world quantitative validation: the real-world evaluation is confined to Physics101 with only single-sample (k=1) MSE against WAN 1.3B, where the overall margin of improvement is modest (28.62 vs 30.08) and WAN outperforms the proposed method on the Fall and Liquid subsets.

Spatial resolution and boundary discretization: spatial downsampling (stride s and patchification r) reduces spatial precision, which can cause boundary bleeding and inaccurate trajectories around fine object boundaries and thin structures.

Short temporal horizon: experiments are restricted to short sequences (16 to 30 frames, corresponding to 1–2 seconds), leaving open the question of whether direct trajectory generation scales well to extended horizons where occlusions and complex multi-object interactions accumulate.

strengths: Compelling motivation and perspective: The paper addresses a foundational question regarding whether video generative models are suitable as physical world models, demonstrating that directly generating point trajectories circumvents pixel synthesis overhead and significantly improves physical plausibility and temporal coherence.

Sound and effective methodology: Formulating dense trajectory forecasting using latent rectified flow / flow matching with factorized spatio-temporal transformer blocks and DINOv2 visual conditioning is clean, well-motivated, and computationally efficient.

Rigorous modality ablation: The controlled experiment in Section 4.3 (Table 6), where the architecture and latent dimensionality are held constant while varying only the output modality (RGB vs. trajectories), provides strong empirical evidence that trajectory space is fundamentally better suited for learning physical dynamics.

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: The authors evaluate across diverse domains (Kubric, LIBERO, Physion, Physics101), benchmark against relevant trajectory predictors (ATM, Tra-MoE, Track2Act) and modern video foundation models (WAN, SVD, LTX), and incorporate a variety of metrics including Best-of-K MSE, FVMD, the rigidity metric LRTL, and a user study.
Extensive efficiency gains: As detailed in Table 19, trajectory generation achieves orders-of-magnitude faster inference and drastically lower memory footprints compared to video diffusion models.
weaknesses: Short temporal horizons: The method is currently demonstrated on relatively short temporal windows (16 to 30 frames, roughly 1–2 seconds), leaving open the question of how trajectory flow matching handles long-horizon accumulation of errors, occlusions, and multi-stage interactions.

Inconsistent benefit of the VAE on real-world data: Ablation results in Table 14 show that the trajectory VAE slightly degrades overall MSE on the real-world Physics101 dataset compared to operating directly on raw coordinates (31.67 vs. 28.62), suggesting that the VAE's compression may introduce spatial blurring or mode behavior that requires clearer trade-off characterization.

Lack of downstream task evaluation: Prior trajectory forecasting works in robotics (e.g., ATM, Tra-MoE) benchmark policy task completion rates. While this work focuses primarily on trajectory fidelity and physical consistency metrics, demonstrating downstream utility (e.g., in visual planning or policy learning) would further substantiate the value of scene-wide dense trajectory prediction.

strengths: Compelling conceptual positioning and clear motivation: the paper challenges the prevailing assumption that large-scale RGB video models are optimal world models for physical forecasting, demonstrating convincingly that generating dense point trajectories directly avoids visual rendering overhead and enforces physical invariants like rigidity and temporal coherence.

Sound and elegant technical formulation: combining a spatio-temporal trajectory VAE with conditional flow matching successfully mitigates the mode collapse issues encountered when diffusing raw coordinates, enabling principled multimodal distribution modeling over possible futures.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation spanning diverse benchmarks: includes physical reasoning and collisions (Kubric, Physion), robotic manipulation (LIBERO), and real-world scenes (Physics101, Cityscapes).

Thorough comparative analysis against both trajectory-based baselines (ATM, Tra-MoE, Track2Act, MotionModes) and fine-tuned state-of-the-art video foundation models (WAN, SVD, DynamicCrafter), supported by well-defined physical consistency metrics (e.g., LRTL) and human user studies.

Insightful ablations and extensions: the paper offers extensive analyses on trajectory grid density, model scaling, the necessity of latent trajectory representation, multi-frame conditioning, and joint video-trajectory diffusion.
weaknesses: Lack of downstream policy evaluation: Prior trajectory-based robotics methods (e.g., ATM, Tra-MoE) evaluate policy execution success on LIBERO; this work restricts LIBERO comparisons to trajectory MSE, leaving it unverified whether the lower trajectory error directly yields higher downstream policy success.

Reliance on pseudo-ground-truth for real-world benchmarks: On Cityscapes and Physics101, evaluations rely on trajectories extracted via CoTracker3, which introduces potential tracking error into both training supervision and benchmark metrics.

Spatial resolution constraints: The predicted trajectory grids are relatively coarse (e.g., 32x32 or 28x56), which can cause inaccuracies around complex occlusion boundaries or on small, thin objects.

strengths: Compelling conceptual positioning: Direct generation of quasi-dense point trajectory grids provides a principled alternative to using high-overhead RGB video diffusion models as world models, naturally respecting temporal continuity and object permanence.

Well-designed technical approach: Utilizing a spatio-temporal VAE combined with latent flow matching and DINOv2 cross-attention allows effective modeling of multimodal future outcomes without suffering from mode collapse.

Comprehensive empirical evaluation: Experiments span diverse synthetic and real-world benchmarks (Kubric, LIBERO, Physion, Physics101, Cityscapes) with comparisons against both regression models (ATM, Tra-MoE), generative trajectory baselines (Track2Act), and fine-tuned video models (WAN, SVD, DynamicCrafter).

Thorough ablations: The manuscript provides insightful ablations validating the importance of latent space modeling over raw coordinate generation, trajectory grid density, and multi-frame conditioning.
weaknesses: Mixed results regarding the trajectory VAE: In Table 16 on the Physics101 dataset, the model without the VAE achieves better overall MSE (28.62 vs. 31.67) than the model with the VAE, which partially contradicts the central motivation that latent space modeling is universally superior.

Potential evaluation bias against video generators: Deriving trajectories from video models using CoTracker3 means that optical flow/tracking failures on generated frames compound the video baseline errors, which may artificially exaggerate the performance gap.

Limitation to 2D coordinates and short horizons: Generating 2D pixel trajectories rather than full 3D motion limits reasoning under severe out-of-plane rotations or occlusions, and the demonstrated horizons remain relatively short (16–30 frames).
Coarse spatial resolution: The model operates on relatively low-density grids (up to 32x32), which can lead to inaccuracies near thin object boundaries and small moving structures.

strengths: Compelling formulation and motivation: casting single-image future motion prediction as dense/quasi-dense point trajectory generation via latent flow matching effectively captures multi-modality and scene-wide physical interactions, moving beyond prior deterministic regressors or sparse goal-conditioned predictors.

Comprehensive and rigorous evaluation: the method is thoroughly validated across varied benchmarks, including robotics manipulation (LIBERO), synthetic physics simulations (Kubric, Physion), real-world physics (Physics101), and driving scenes (Cityscapes), alongside an ELO-ranked user study.

Insightful analysis of video generators vs. trajectory models: the paper provides compelling empirical evidence showing that state-of-the-art video generation models (e.g., WAN, SVD) struggle with physical plausibility and temporal consistency due to pixel synthesis overhead, whereas direct trajectory generation achieves superior motion fidelity at a fraction of the compute and parameter cost.

Extensive ablation studies: the experiments carefully investigate key design choices, including the role of the trajectory VAE latent space in preventing mode collapse, the impact of grid sampling density, model scaling, and natural extensions to multi-frame conditioning.

Promising downstream application: demonstrating that joint diffusion of RGB and trajectory latents improves physical plausibility (e.g., rigidity) of synthesized video adds practical value to the video generation community.
weaknesses: Reliance on pseudo ground truth for real-world datasets: on Physics101 and Cityscapes, evaluation depends heavily on trajectories extracted via CoTracker3, which may inherit tracker failure modes or biases into the evaluation metrics.

Limited temporal horizon and spatial resolution: the model is currently trained on relatively short sequences (16 to 30 frames) on coarse grids (up to 32x32), which may limit its applicability to longer-term planning and fine-grained motion along intricate object boundaries.

Inconsistent VAE impact on real-world data: as shown in Table 16, using the VAE slightly degrades overall MSE on Physics101 compared to raw coordinate prediction, suggesting that latent trajectory modeling benefits may depend on the availability of multi-modal ground truth.
